newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Gdansk refinery cuts diesel sales by 30 pct.
newsitem.headline: Polish Gdansk refinery cuts diesel sales by 30 pct.

text.p: Poland's second largest refinery in Gdansk said on Thursday it will cut its monthly diesel fuel sales by 30 percent to 80,000 tonnes in September because imports are too costly after recent world oil price rises.
The refinery has been selling 120,000 tonnes of diesel a month, of which it produced 80,000 tonnes itself and imported the remaining 40,000 tonnes.
Polish fuel prices are set by the finance ministry, which, despite rising world prices, does not want to allow domestic rises to avoid the strong inflationary impluse they would create.
"So far we imported the 40,000 tonnes, but the rise of world oil prices make this unprofitable. This might lead to shortages on the domestic market," refinery spokeswoman Ewa Sielicka told Reuters.
She added that a duty-free fuel import quota set by the government would help ease the shortage.
On Wednesday deputy industry minister Roman Czerwinski said Poland may have to use state reserves of diesel and introduce duty-free import quotas to offset shortages.
Czerwinski said duty-free import quotas for 300,000 tonnes of gasoline and 400,000 tonnes of diesel may be needed to stabilise the market unless world oil prices fall.
